beats.narration: Module four, wrapped. Five takeaways, one per layer. Same test as always: if you can explain each one to a teammate, it's yours.

One: set the standard before you build. The eval turns done into a score, the grader matches the output's shape, and the judge is calibrated against human labels before it's trusted. Two: match the test to the failure, and trace to localize — most silent breaks live at the integration seam where two passing components hand off. Three: sort every failure first. Retriable gets backoff with a cap, terminal fails fast, and tool errors come back flagged, never empty. Four: measure cost per call, and fan out only when the task truly splits — fifteen times the tokens buys nothing on coupled work. Five: treat fetched content as data and enforce the boundary with a hook, because least privilege is what bounds a steered agent.

items.text: 1. set the standard first — eval, matched grader, calibrated judge
2. test per failure + trace — breaks live at the seams
3. sort failures — backoff retriable · fail-fast terminal · flag tool errors
4. measure per call — fan out only when work truly splits (15×!)
5. fetched content = data — hooks + least privilege bound the agent
